mappings.evidence: When it’s in the up position, the light is on (like “true”).
When it’s down, the light is off (like “false”).
The switch can only be in one of two positions; there’s no middle ground—just on or off.

result.process_summary: Both the light switch and a Boolean value toggle between exactly two mutually exclusive states. The switch’s physical positions (up/down) map directly onto the logical truth values (true/false), and the act of flipping the switch mirrors the operation of changing a Boolean’s value.
potential_breaks: A simple switch is assumed to have only two positions; real switches may have intermediate or dimmer settings, which introduces more than two states, unlike a Boolean.
Physical failure (e.g., a burnt‑out bulb) can make the light’s state ambiguous, whereas a Boolean value is always well‑defined.
